Read the transcript of the audio guide
  1. A Bavarian immigrant who sold cloth out of a San Francisco storefront put his name on a pair of work trousers reinforced with copper rivets. source
  2. Levi Strauss was born Löb Strauß on 26 February 1829 in Buttenheim, a village in the Kingdom of Bavaria, into a Jewish family. source
  3. In 1847, with his mother and sisters, he emigrated to the United States, sailing from Bremerhaven. source
  4. In New York he joined the dry-goods business run by his older brothers and learned the trade of importing and selling cloth and household goods. source
  5. He became a United States citizen in 1853 and, like tens of thousands of others, turned his eyes west toward the California gold rush. source
  6. He did not dig for gold; he sold to the people who did, and to everyone who came to feed and clothe them. source
  7. In the early 1870s a tailor in Reno, Nevada, named Jacob Davis, one of Strauss's cloth customers, worked out a way to keep work trousers from tearing at the pocket corners and fly: he fastened the stress points with copper rivets. source
  8. The idea worked, and his customers wanted more, but Davis could not afford the seventy-dollar fee to patent it. source
  9. Strauss agreed to finance it. source
  10. On 20 May 1873 the United States granted Patent No. 139,121 to Jacob Davis, "assignor to himself and Levi Strauss & Company." source
  11. The patent names Davis first, as the inventor. In his words: source
  12. My invention relates to a fastening for pocket-openings, whereby the sewed seams are prevented from ripping. source
  13. Strauss endowed scholarships at the University of California and supported orphanages and Jewish charities in the city. source
  14. When people make something together, how should the credit be shared?
Read the transcript of the short and the video
  1. Levi Strauss was born Löb Strauß in Bavaria in 1829 and came to the United States as a teenager in 1847. source
  2. In New York he joined the dry-goods business run by his older brothers and learned the trade of importing and selling cloth and household goods. source
  3. He became a United States citizen in 1853. source
  4. He built a dry-goods business in gold-rush San Francisco, and in 1873 he and the tailor Jacob Davis patented the riveted work trouser — the blue jean. source
  5. The blue jean was a joint invention: the rivet idea was Jacob Davis's. source
  6. Strauss was the partner who financed and manufactured it, not the lone genius of popular legend. source
  7. An immigrant's name became a word spoken in every country on earth. source
  8. Read the full story, with every source, on this page.
